solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The same artist's not in Radio Times cutting

indicators.note: the pair of Ts cuts into what is left of Radio, sitting inside it
the artist is not in the word Radio, so those two letters are dropped from it

parts.note: taken as the word itself, before the artist is removed
RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword artist
T is short for time, so two of them, Times, give a pair of Ts

explanation.surface: A painter is missing from a clipping taken out of the Radio Times listings magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radio Times' is a British TV listings magazine, but here the words split; 'Times' gives two Ts because T is short for time, and 's not in' drops the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is the word written in a list to mean a repeat of what stands above.

clue.text: Dud politicians who in Paris stop poor tipping

indicators.note: the politicians and the French word stop up the gap inside the overturned word
tipping over turns the word for poor back to front

parts.note: poor quality is bad
MPs are Members of Parliament
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: Useless politicians, the 'who' of Paris, plug a gap in poor tipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipping' reverses BAD to DAB, and MPSQUI goes in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp squib is a firework that fails to go off, hence anything that is a disappointing dud.

clue.text: More than one current change, that is, ending on top

indicators.note: change says the Latin phrase is altered in a stated way
in a down entry the final letter moves to the top, the first place

parts.note: id est, the Latin behind i.e., means that is

explanation.surface: Several flows alter, eventually finishing at the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change, ... ending on top' moves the last letter T of ID EST to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides are the regular currents of the sea, so the plural fits more than one.

clue.text: I run mad occasionally in public haunt in old Chinatown?

indicators.note: these letters are placed in the word for public

parts.note: open means public, available to all

indicators.note: occasionally takes only some of the letters, every other one of run mad

explanation.surface: Someone admits to going wild now and then in a public spot in an old Chinese quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' gives UMD, the even letters of 'run mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium dens were places where people smoked the drug, a notorious haunt in old London's Chinatown.

clue.text: Wild uproar about Tory leader has America very happy

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, around, the leading letter of Tory
wild suggests the letters of uproar run out of control into a new order
leader points to the first letter of the word Tory

explanation.surface: A rowdy scene around a Conservative chief delights the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' reshuffles the fodder to RAPUROU, and 'about' puts the leading T of Tory inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapturous describes delight so great it carries a person away, a synonym for very happy.

clue.text: Service engineers set about computer systems

indicators.note: the engineers are set about, around, the other piece

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
IT, information technology, covers computer systems

explanation.surface: Maintenance technicians start work on the computers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like maintenance; it is a religious ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a ceremonial act, such as a religious service.

clue.text: Hairy pet for each Welsh girl on boat

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
Sian is a Welsh girl's name
a cat is a catamaran or a cat-boat, a kind of sailing boat

explanation.surface: A long-haired pet belongs to every Welsh girl on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Persian is a breed of cat famous for its long, thick fur.

clue.text: Cheerful, United lead Polish off

parts.note: U is short for United, as in football club names
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
to polish off food is to eat it all

explanation.surface: A football side's lead is wiped out, yet the mood stays upbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal, not a winning margin; 'Polish off' is to finish eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means optimistic and positive, a synonym for cheerful.

clue.text: Reveals quiet study, fully extended

parts.note: to out someone is to reveal their secret
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Someone exposes a calm piece of research that was stretched out completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Outspread means spread out wide, so stretched to its full extent.

clue.text: It bears a stigma, part of nasty lesion

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mark of shame is carried by part of an ugly sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stigma' suggests disgrace, but here it is the botanical stigma of a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: In a flower the style is the stalk of the pistil, which carries the stigma at its tip.

clue.text: I'd take temperature in sea at Calais around solstice

indicators.note: the run of pieces sits in the French sea, inside its letters

parts.note: mer is the French word for sea, as spoken in Calais
ID is the contraction without its apostrophe
to win a prize is to take it

explanation.surface: Someone plans to check the water temperature off the French coast at the shortest day of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea at Calais' calls for the French MER, which holds IDWINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Midwinter is the time of year around the December solstice, the shortest day.

clue.text: Horse keeps dry round the bend

indicators.note: the horse keeps the other piece, holding it within

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
TT, teetotal, means not drinking, dry

explanation.surface: A horse holds back from water, or stays dry, as it rounds a bend on the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the bend' is British slang for mad, not a turn in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Round the bend is informal for crazy, and batty is a synonym for crazy.

clue.text: Oil supplier spreading a mess close to drive

indicators.note: spreading the letters of a mess about puts them in a new order
close to means the closing letter of the word drive

explanation.surface: Oil from a car leaks, spreading a mess near the driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil supplier' suggests a garage or a refinery; it is a plant whose seeds are pressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame seeds are pressed to yield a cooking oil, so the plant supplies it.

clue.text: City anger inspires good software

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the anger takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: bile is ill temper, anger
an app is a piece of software

explanation.surface: Annoyance drives the creation of a fine computer program for a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Apple is the nickname for New York City.

clue.text: Energy's reduced — check period and switch cover?

parts.note: E for energy, with the 's giving S
cut means reduced, as in cut prices
CH is the chess notation for check
an eon is a very long period of time

explanation.surface: Power is cut back: inspect the timer and replace the switch cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch cover?' is a definition by example: the escutcheon is the plate round a keyhole or light switch.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is a protective plate fitted around a keyhole, handle or switch.

clue.text: Mean peacekeepers to gather round hospital

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: the folding word goes round the hospital, enclosing it

parts.note: to pleat cloth is to gather it in folds
SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital

explanation.surface: UN troops are set to assemble around a hospital in a nasty situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb or an average; here it is the adjective, nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the sense of unkind or nasty is a synonym for unpleasant.

clue.text: Tip bucket one held in sink

parts.note: to bucket down is to pour with rain

indicators.note: the numeral is held in the drilling word, inside its letters

parts.note: to sink a well or shaft is to bore it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone tips a bucket and finds an item stuck in the sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' means a gratuity; a pourboire is the French word, used in English, for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pourboire, literally 'for drinking', is a French term for a gratuity given to a waiter.

clue.text: I leave to exercise joint

indicators.note: the letter I is told to leave, to go out of the word

parts.note: to wield power is to exercise it

explanation.surface: Someone excuses themselves to go and work out a stiff joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A weld is a joint made by fusing metal pieces together with heat.

clue.text: No boarding here in cool shady ground

indicators.note: ground as in crushed and broken up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: No timber planks are laid on this cool, shady patch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as land, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A day school teaches pupils who go home each evening, so none stay as boarders.

clue.text: I follow stuff about English or Chinese character maybe

indicators.note: the following word goes about the English letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
to ram something in is to stuff it

explanation.surface: I trail some English material, or perhaps Chinese text.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideogram is a written symbol representing an idea, as many Chinese characters do.

clue.text: Obscure endless stuff on jacket?

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a blurb is the promotional text printed on a book's dust jacket

explanation.surface: Something unclear about never-ending writing on a book cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jacket' is a book's dust jacket, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To blur something is to make it indistinct, to obscure it.

clue.text: He pays for company guards trained to count yen

indicators.note: trained suggests the guards are drilled into a new formation, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to add up is to count
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A business has its security staff taught to count Japanese money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' reads as a firm, but the definition means companionship paid for.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar daddy is an older man who lavishes money on a younger partner in return for companionship.

clue.text: Check cheese is picked up

indicators.note: picked up as by a microphone, meaning heard rather than read

parts.note: feta is a Greek white cheese

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the cheese as it is lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent FETA and the answer are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To fetter is to restrain with chains, so to check or curb movement.

clue.text: A doctor in church nurses European character

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the pieces before take the European inside

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A medic in a church looks after a European patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here but the letters IN; 'nurses' places E within INCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambience is the atmosphere or distinctive character of a place.

clue.text: Old Greek version of 'Room at the Top'?

definitions.meaning: relating to ancient Athens and its dialect
a loft space just under the roof, playing on the title of the novel

explanation.surface: A Greek translation of the novel 'Room at the Top'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room at the Top' is John Braine's 1957 novel; taken literally it is the top room of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic means of ancient Athens, and an attic is the room under a roof.

clue.text: Funny guy collects Sierra from space

indicators.note: the comedian collects the letter, taking it in

parts.note: a comic is a comedian, a funny man
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A comedian picks up someone named Sierra, arriving from space.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmic means relating to the cosmos, the universe, so coming from outer space.

clue.text: Dug stuff up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: stuff is an old word for cloth, and denim is a cloth

explanation.surface: Someone excavated some things and brought them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' means fabric here.
explanation.definitionFit: Mined means excavated from the ground, the past tense of dig in that sense.

clue.text: It's used in fencing sheep, evenly erected

indicators.note: erected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the answer sits in the words, fenced in by them, so its letters are concealed within the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something is used for enclosing sheep, set up level.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave no word for the hiding; 'in fencing' does that job while also pointing at the sport, so the bare definition is 'It's used', made fair by the sword sense of fencing.
explanation.definitionFit: The epee is one of the three swords used in the sport of fencing, so a thing used there.

clue.text: Hint of disgrace? It's not said commonly?

definitions.meaning: a stain or trace of shame on a reputation
a dialect contraction of it is not

explanation.surface: A suggestion of scandal, or a phrase that common folk don't use.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of corruption, and 'tain't is folksy speech for it isn't.

clue.text: Guide operates with northern language

indicators.note: guide in the sense of steer, directing the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A tour guide works in a northern dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guide' looks like a noun naming a person; it is a verb telling the solver to rearrange OPERATES plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is the constructed international language devised by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: Green light in spare room

definitions.meaning: the space left free above or around something, headroom

explanation.surface: Permission is given to use a spare bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare room' suggests a guest bedroom; here it is a gap left over, as under a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance means both official approval to proceed and the space allowing something to pass.

clue.text: Gong duke going into dinner, say

indicators.note: the duke's letter goes into the meal

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: A gong is sounded as a duke goes in for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gong' is British slang for a medal or decoration, not the dinner gong the surface paints.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal usage a gong is an award or decoration, such as a medal.
